predecessors.note: Abu Zakariya, 'initially appointed governor of the region by the Almohad caliph', declared himself independent in 1229 (infobox 'Established: 1229'); he annexed Constantine and Bejaia in 1230 and took Algiers in 1235.

successors.note: Infobox 'Ottoman conquest: 1574' (Ottoman Tunisia); Tripoli fell to the Ottomans in 1551 (Ottoman Tripolitania). Cliopatria's Hafsid row stops in 1571.

land.text: Constantine's 'definitive attachment to the central power of Algiers in the 1530s'; Bejaia taken from the Spanish by Salah Reis in 1555

successors.note: Infobox successor 'Regency of Algiers'. Cliopatria's Regency row starts only in 1706.
Infobox successor 'Spanish Tripoli'; Bejaia was also Spanish from 1509 until 1555.

capitals.name: Tunis
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Tunis'. After 1277 a western branch ruled from Bejaia and Constantine ('another branch ruled from Bejaia (Bijaya) and Constantine (Qusantina) in the west'); the page dates neither seat.

rulers.name: Muhammad V (Moulay Hasan)
rulers.note: Ousted by Barbarossa in August 1534 and restored as a Spanish client in July 1535 (Conquest of Tunis page).

rulers.name: Muhammad VI
rulers.note: 'Muhammad VI, the last Caliph of the Hafsids'.

correction.text: Tunisia, with Constantine and Bejaia from 1230

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1229-1235: Cliopatria's Hafsid row starts in 1236. 'Established: 1229'; Constantine and Bejaia were annexed in 1230; Algiers 'as far as the Chelif River' in 1235 (ledger). The infobox gives no area.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1236 Hafsid shape without Tripolitania, which the Hafsids annex in 1401 and 1458

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria draws 224,040 km2: Tunisia (311 cells), the Constantinois (249) and Tripolitania (162). The page dates the annexation of Tripoli to 1401 and the conquest of Tripolitania to 1458, so the correction removes Tripolitania for the early centuries. The page has no area figure, so the infobox comparison cannot be made.

Same shape as 1236 (224,190 km2); same correction. After al-Mustansir's death in 1277 the page has the dynasty split between Tunis and a western branch at Bejaia and Constantine, 'reunified under Abu Yahya Abu Bakr II' (1318-1346); the ledger carries it.
Same shape (224,295 km2); same correction. The Marinids 'entered Tunis in September 1347' and left in 1349 (ledger).

correction.text: the Hafsid land of 1344 without Tripolitania, 1352-1362

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 1352-1362, years Cliopatria gives to the Marinid Sultanate's 737,941 km2 shape (which contains all of Hafsid Ifriqiya). The pages do not support that: Abu Inan 'took Bejaia in 1353' and 'took Tunis in 1357, becoming master of Ifrikiya' but 'was forced to retreat from Tunisia in 1357'; Abu Ishaq Ibrahim II ruled at Tunis 1350-1369. The correction is the Hafsid shape of 1344 without Tripolitania; the Marinid occupations of Bejaia (1353-1358) and Tunis (August-late 1357) are ledger events.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1363 Hafsid shape without Tripolitania, valid to 1400

keyframe_review.note: Same 224,190 km2 shape. The Hafsid page has 'the emir of Bejaia and Constantine' conquer Tunis in 1370 and Abu Faris annex Tripoli (1401), reoccupy Gafsa (1401), Biskra (1402) and Tozeur (1404); the shape is right for 1363-1400 without Tripolitania, and the ledger adds Tripoli in 1401.

224,190 km2, Tunisia, the Constantinois and Tripolitania: right once Tripolitania is back ('Uthman conquered Tripolitania in 1458'; Tripoli annexed 1401) and until Spain takes Bejaia (1509) and Tripoli (1510), which the ledger records. For 1453-1457 Tripolitania is early by the page. The page gives no area.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1512 Hafsid shape without Bejaia (1509) and Tripoli (1510), both Spanish

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria barely changes the shape in 1512 (222,431 km2: 7 cells lost) although the Spanish had taken Bejaia in 1509 and Tripoli in 1510 (Regency of Algiers page: 'The Spanish took Bejaia from the Hafsids in 1509, and Tripoli in 1510'). The correction removes both cities.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1521 Hafsid shape without Bejaia and Tripoli

keyframe_review.note: 222,305 km2: same correction as 1512; Algiers is taken in 1520 and lost in 1525 (ledger) and is outside Cliopatria's shape (its western edge is 4.45 E, east of Algiers at 3.06 E).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1534 Hafsid shape without the Constantinois, Bejaia and Tripoli

keyframe_review.note: 221,486 km2 (4 cells fewer than 1521, in the Tunis area, back in 1540: the researcher reads this as Cliopatria's mark of Barbarossa's occupation of August 1534 and Charles V's of July 1535). Constantine 'liberated itself from the Hafsid Emirate of Bejaia in the early 16th century' and its 'definitive attachment to the central power of Algiers' came 'in the 1530s' (Beylik of Constantine page; infobox 'Established: 1528'), so the Constantinois should leave the Hafsid shape. The correction removes the Constantinois, Bejaia and Tripoli.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1540 Hafsid shape without the Constantinois, Bejaia and Tripoli

keyframe_review.note: 222,305 km2: same correction as 1534; the Hafsid sultan Muhammad V is a Spanish client at Tunis from July 1535 (Conquest of Tunis page).

correction.text: Tunisia, the Hafsid land that remained

keyframe_review.note: 173,148 km2: Cliopatria drops Tripolitania in 1552. The Siege of Tripoli page has Tripoli 'under Spanish rule since its capture in 1510', then the Knights Hospitaller's from 1530, and 'Tripoli capitulated on 14 August 1551' to the Ottomans, so the Hafsids did not lose it in 1551; the page does not mention the Hafsids at all. The correction is Tunisia alone (Cliopatria's 1556 shape).

88,079 km2, Tunisia alone: right for 1556-1563 (Tunis a Spanish client under Ahmad III, 1543-1569). The infobox gives no area. The Algerian part left the shape in 1556 against 1509-1530s in the pages (see 1512 and 1534).

Shape unchanged (88,079 km2) but it holds to 1574, not 1571: 'The Ottomans conquered Tunis again in 1569 and held it for four years'; 'Don Juan of Austria recaptured it in 1573'; 'The Ottomans reconquered Tunis in 1574, and Muhammad VI, the last Caliph of the Hafsids' fell. Tunisia was occupied 1569-1573 (ledger).

ledger.note: 1229: Abu Zakariya makes Ifriqiya independent of the Almohads. Governor 'initially appointed ... by the Almohad caliph before declaring his independence'; 'A year later, in 1229, al-Ma'mun officially renounced' Ibn Tumart's doctrine and 'Abu Zakariya used this as a pretext to repudiate his authority and to declare himself independent'; infobox 'Established: 1229'. He took the title Amir al-Mu'minin only in 1236 or 1237. The page names the region only as 'the region'; Tunisia is the researcher's reading.
1230: Abu Zakariya annexes Constantine and Bejaia. 'Abu Zakariya annexed Constantine (Qusantina) and Bejaia (Bijaya) in 1230.'

region.text: Algiers as far as the Chelif River

ledger.note: 1235: the Hafsids take Algiers as far as the Chelif. 'In 1235 he captured Algiers and then established his authority as far as the Chelif River'; the page does not say from whom. Cliopatria's Hafsid shape starts east of Algiers (4.4 E) and gives the area to the Zayyanids.

1242: Abu Zakariya takes Tlemcen from the Zayyanids. 'In 1242, he captured Tlemcen from the Zayyanids'; the Zayyanid page has their kingdom 'intermittently a vassal of Hafsid Ifriqiya, Marinid Morocco, or Aragon', so the capture is drawn as an occupation of the city, not an annexation (the page gives no later event).
1249: the Hafsid hold on Tlemcen ends, bridging. The page is silent on when Zayyanid independence returned; 5 October 1249 is Abu Zakariya's death (ruler table).

ledger.counterpart: Hafsid branch of Bejaia and Constantine
ledger.note: 1277: the dynasty splits in two. After al-Mustansir's death in 1277 the page has the dynasty divide 'between Tunis and a western branch based in Bejaia and Constantine'.

ledger.counterpart: Hafsid branch of Bejaia and Constantine
ledger.note: 1318: the western branch is reunified with Tunis 'under Abu Yahya Abu Bakr II' (r. 1318-1346). The page gives no year for the reunification; 1318 is the start of his reign.

September 1347: Abu al-Hasan's Marinids enter Tunis. 'In a campaign in early 1347, Abu al-Hasan's Moroccan army swept through Ifriqiya' and 'entered Tunis in September 1347'; the Hafsid page: 'He conquered Tunis in 1347 and the Hafsid governors in the region accepted his authority.'
1349: the Marinids leave Ifriqiya. 'Abu al-Hasan was forced to return west in 1349' (the Arab tribes had defeated his army near Kairouan in April 1348).
1353: Abu Inan takes Bejaia. 'He took Bejaia in 1353'; he had retaken Tlemcen in 1352.

August 1357: Abu Inan takes Tunis. He 'captured Tunis in August 1357, but he was soon forced by his own troops to abandon the region'; the Abu Inan page: he 'took Tunis in 1357, becoming master of Ifrikiya'. [Review af-02-d: month dropped and event placed before the 1357 retreat so that the start precedes its end; the month (August) stays in this note.]
1357: Abu Inan retreats from Tunisia. 'He was forced to retreat from Tunisia in 1357' after his vizier's intrigues; he fell ill in November 1357.

1358: Marinid Bejaia, bridging. The page gives no date for the loss of Bejaia; 10 January 1358 is Abu Inan's strangling, the end of the Marinid hold on the central Maghreb. The Hafsid page has 'the emir of Bejaia and Constantine' in the west by 1370.
1370: the emir of Bejaia and Constantine takes Tunis and reunites the Hafsid lands. 'The emir of Bejaia and Constantine, conquered Tunis in 1370'; Ahmad II reigns 1370-1394.
1401: Abu Faris annexes Tripoli. 'He annexed Tripoli (1401) and Algiers (1410-1411)'. The page does not name the previous holder; 'nobody' marks that Tripoli was not another dossier's state.
1401: Abu Faris reoccupies Gafsa. 'He reoccupied Tozeur (1404), Gafsa (1401), and Biskra (1402).' The page names no other holder.
1402: Abu Faris reoccupies Biskra.
1404: Abu Faris reoccupies Tozeur.

1410-1411: Abu Faris annexes Algiers. 'He annexed Tripoli (1401) and Algiers (1410-1411)'; the page does not name the holder (Cliopatria's Zayyanid shape contains Algiers, but no Zayyanid page says so), so the counterpart is 'nobody' and the Zayyanid dossier writes no loss.

1424: Abu Faris beats the Zayyanid sultan and installs a client. 'In 1424, he defeated the Zayyanid sultan, Abu Malik Abd al-Wahid', who 'was eventually replaced by yet another Zayyanid relative with Abu Faris Abd al-Aziz's help in 1431'.
1434: Hafsid influence over Tlemcen ends, bridging. The page is silent on the end; 1434 is the end of Abu Faris's reign ('the apogee of Hafsid power and prosperity').
1458: Uthman conquers Tripolitania. 'Uthman conquered Tripolitania in 1458 and appointed a governor in Ouargla in 1463.' The page does not name the previous holder.
1463: Uthman appoints a governor at Ouargla in the Sahara (same sentence as 1458); a governor, not a province boundary.
1509: Spain takes Bejaia. 'The Spanish took Bejaia from the Hafsids in 1509' (the page's entry covers 1509-1510 and puts Tripoli in 1510).
1510: Spain takes Tripoli. 'and Tripoli in 1510'; the Siege of Tripoli page: 'under Spanish rule since its capture in 1510'.
1520: the Hafsids and Kuku take Algiers. They 'blockaded Algiers and took it in 1520'; Hayreddin 'retook Algiers' in 1525.
1525: Hayreddin retakes Algiers. 'Hayreddin retook Algiers after defeating Ahmad ibn al-Kadi' (Kuku); the page does not say that the Hafsids still held it.

1530s: Constantine passes to Algiers. 'Its definitive attachment to the central power of Algiers in the 1530s' (infobox 'Established: 1528'; it 'liberated itself from the Hafsid Emirate of Bejaia in the early 16th century'). The decade is the page's; 1530 is the researcher's bridging year.
16 August 1534: Barbarossa takes Tunis. He 'conquered Tunis on 16 August 1534' and ousted Muley Hasan (Muhammad V).

region.text: La Goulette, the port of Tunis

ledger.note: 1535: a Spanish garrison holds La Goulette. Charles 'left a garrison under Bernardino de Mendoza' (undated sentence, after July 1535); Tunis 'remained under Spanish control until its Ottoman recapture in 1569'. The Hafsids stay on the throne as Spanish vassals.

21 July 1535: Charles V enters Tunis. 'Charles entered Tunis on July 21' after taking La Goulette; Muley Hasan was 'restored as client ruler of Tunis' and 'signed a treatise restoring Tunis' vassalage to Spain'.

region.text: La Goulette, the port of Tunis

ledger.note: 1569: the Ottomans take Tunis from the Spanish. 'The Ottomans recaptured the city in 1569'; Uluj Ali 'captured Tunis from Spain's Hafsid vassals in 1569' (Regency of Algiers page).
1569: the Ottomans hold Tunis for four years. 'The Ottomans again conquered Tunis in 1569 and held it for four years.'
1573: Don Juan of Austria retakes Tunis. 'Don Juan of Austria recaptured it in 1573'; Muhammad VI reigns 1573-1574.
1573: Spain holds Tunis a second time. 'Spain captured it again in 1573' 'only to lose it again in 1574'.
1574: the Ottomans end the Spanish hold.

1574: the Ottomans take Tunis and the Hafsid dynasty ends. 'The Ottomans reconquered Tunis in 1574, and Muhammad VI, the last Caliph of the Hafsids' fell (infobox 'Ottoman conquest: 1574'). Cliopatria ends the row in 1571.

wars.name: Hafsid expansion into Algeria and Tlemcen
wars.outcome: Hafsid gains: Constantine and Bejaia 1230, Algiers to the Chelif 1235, Tlemcen 1242.

wars.name: Marinid invasion of Ifriqiya
wars.outcome: Marinid occupation: Tunis September 1347; the Arab tribes defeat Abu al-Hasan near Kairouan in April 1348; he withdraws in 1349.

wars.name: Abu Inan's conquest of the central Maghreb
wars.outcome: Marinid gains that did not last: Bejaia 1353, Tunis August 1357, abandoned the same year; Abu Inan strangled on 10 January 1358.

wars.name: Abu Faris's campaigns
wars.outcome: Hafsid gains: Tripoli 1401, Gafsa 1401, Biskra 1402, Tozeur 1404, Algiers 1410-1411; the Zayyanid sultan beaten in 1424 and replaced in 1431.

wars.name: Spanish conquests of Bejaia and Tripoli
wars.outcome: Spanish victory: Bejaia taken in 1509 and Tripoli in 1510.
wars.note: Bejaia stayed Spanish until Salah Reis took it in 1555.

wars.name: Hafsid and Kuku war against Algiers
wars.outcome: The Hafsids and Kuku take Algiers in 1520; Hayreddin retakes it in 1525.

wars.name: Ottoman-Habsburg struggle for Tunis
wars.outcome: Barbarossa takes Tunis 16 August 1534; Charles V retakes it 21 July 1535 and restores Muley Hasan as a Spanish client; the Ottomans retake it in 1569, Don Juan of Austria in 1573, the Ottomans finally in 1574.
wars.note: Conquest of Tunis (1535) page for 1534-1535; Hafsid dynasty page for 1569-1574.

certainty.note: No treaty line is given on any page; the Saharan edge and the Tripolitanian and Algerian frontiers are approximate throughout. The coastal cities (Tunis, Bejaia, Tripoli) are firm points.

sources.title: Abu Inan Faris

notes: CLIOPATRIA. (1) Row 1236-1571 against the page's 1229-1574. (2) Tripolitania (162 cells) is in every shape from 1236 to 1551; the page has Tripoli annexed in 1401 and Tripolitania conquered in 1458, Spain taking Tripoli in 1510, the Knights holding it from 1530 and the Ottomans taking it on 14 August 1551 (Siege of Tripoli page, which never mentions the Hafsids). (3) The Constantinois is in every shape to 1555 although Bejaia was Spanish from 1509 and Constantine Algerian in the 1530s. (4) The 1352-1362 gap is filled by the Marinid row's 737,941 km2 shape, which the pages do not support: the Marinids held Bejaia 1353-1358 and Tunis for months of 1357. (5) Algiers (taken 1235, 1410-1411, 1520) lies west of the Hafsid shape's 4.4 E edge. AREA. The Hafsid page has no area figure; no infobox comparison was possible. NOT SETTLED. Who held Tripoli, Gafsa, Biskra, Tozeur and Ouargla before the Hafsid annexations (recorded as 'nobody'); the dates of the 1277 split and 1318 reunification (the page gives the death of al-Mustansir and the reign of Abu Bakr II only); the Kingdom of Kuku, the Banu Abbas, Djerba (1423, tagged [citation needed] on the page), the Hafsid vassalage of the Zayyanids and of Tunis to Spain (1535-1574) as dated tints; the Spanish presence at Bejaia 1509-1555 and at Tripoli 1510-1530 (Spanish dossiers). The page gives 1236 or 1237 for the adoption of the title Amir al-Mu'minin; no event was written. COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER: 'Hafsid branch of Bejaia and Constantine' and 'Hafsid branch of Tunis' (internal branches); regency-of-algiers has a Cliopatria row only from 1706, the Algiers dossier is another batch's; Kuku is not in Cliopatria.
